Unit 2 • HL

Systems Control

Introduction

How do machines manage chaos and control the physical world?

This unit focuses on two critical HL concepts: Concurrency (how OSs manage multiple tasks without crashing) and Control (how computers sense and change the physical world). You will master the logic of Feedback Loops and understand the dangers of Deadlock.

You'll start by looking at the Operating System's struggle to manage competing resources (Multitasking). Then you'll move to physical computing, defining the Input-Process-Output cycle of Sensors and Actuators, determining when to use Open-Loop vs Closed-Loop logic.

Multitasking & Deadlock

When multiple programs want the same resource, chaos can ensue.

  • Resource Contention: Processes fighting for CPU/Memory.
  • Deadlock: A standstill where Process A waits for B, and B waits for A. (The "Dining Philosophers" problem).

Control Systems Structure

Automated systems follow a strict Hardware-Software loop:

  1. Sensor: Detects physical data (Heat, Light).
  2. Transducer: Converts physics to electricity (ADC).
  3. Controller: The CPU/Logic that makes a decision.
  4. Actuator: The muscle that creates movement/change (Motor, Heater).

Feedback Loops

Does the system know if it succeeded?

  • Open-Loop: Input -> Process -> Output. (No checking. e.g., Cheap Toaster, Sprinkler).
  • Closed-Loop: Input -> Process -> Output -> Feedback -> Adjust. (Self-correcting. e.g., Thermostat, Cruise Control).

Key Terminology
TermDefinition
MultitaskingThe ability of an OS to execute more than one task simultaneously (via time-slicing).
DeadlockA situation where two or more processes are unable to proceed because each is waiting for the other to release a resource.
SensorA device that detects or measures a physical property and records, indicates, or otherwise responds to it.
ActuatorA component of a machine that is responsible for moving and controlling a mechanism or system.
TransducerA device that converts variations in a physical quantity (like pressure) into an electrical signal (or vice versa).
FeedbackInformation about the output of a system that is returned to the input to modify the next action.
Open-Loop SystemA control system where the output has no influence or effect on the control action.
Closed-Loop SystemA control system that uses feedback to maintain a desired output.

Common Misconceptions

Deadlock is just Lag

Thinking the computer is just slow. Deadlock is a fatal logic freeze. Unless the OS kills a process, it will wait FOREVER.

Sensors do the work

Thinking the thermometer heats the room. The Sensor MEASURES. The Actuator (Heater) DOES the work.

Open-Loop is 'Bad'

Assuming Closed-Loop is always better. Open-loop is simpler and cheaper. Your toaster doesn't need a laser-scan of the bread; a timer is enough.

Syllabus Coverage

  • A1.3.5 Multitasking & Deadlock
  • A1.3.6 Control Systems (Sensors/Actuators)
  • A1.3.7 Loop Types (Open/Closed)

Real-World Uses

  • Autonomous Vehicles (Lidar/Steering)
  • Smart Home Thermostats
  • Industrial Robots
  • Traffic Light Systems
  • Fly-by-wire Aircraft

Think Deeper

"Who is the Knower?" When a self-driving car (Closed-Loop) makes a split-second decision to swerve to save a life, who made that decision? The programmer years ago, or the algorithm in the moment?
